Hi [~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] please confirm the question raised by Natalia, thanks.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Irish rider ([profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/250855142/overview]).On 16 June, wrote to CS ([link|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/593069101]) claiming a data breach given that “_one your team members shared my personal data of domestic violence to guardian police and completely fabricated a story_”. No additional context provided.
* Based on internal investigation:
** On 20 May 2025, rider complained about driver who did not show up ([link|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/576652211]). On the thread, rider mentioned “_I fleeing domestic violence and very vulnerable at present_”. As a result of this, the CS Safety Team seems to have reported the incident to the police ([link|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/577285962]).
*** Report includes rider’s name, phone number and email address. Report is brief, and mainly says “_They mentioned that they were fleeing domestic violence and were vulnerable… Bolt is reporting this matter to the police as an allegation of crime has been reported to Bolt._” As such, no embellishment - just repeating what they said.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* This is not a personal data breach. This is Bolt CS Safety understandably reporting an allegation of a crime to the police.
** We have written evidence to show that the rider claimed they were fleeing domestic violence. Bolt in no way added nor embellished the rider’s account, and so has not fabricated the story.  By making the police report, Bolt was acting reasonably as a responsible platform owner. There is also nothing to suggest that the rider has suffered any harm here.
*** NB. Across other Beehive ticket’s, the rider’s tone has been generally combative on various issues. As such, this could just be a case of a user being difficult.
** No need to report to the ODPO, as no confirmed data incident.
* Bolt is entitled to share information with the police in this context.
** *Purpose*: To cooperate with law enforcement and protect our users.
** *Legal basis*:
*** (i) *Article 6*: Legitimate interest. There is no statutory obligation under Irish law to report suspected domestic violence to the police.
*** (ii) *Article 10*: The information concerns alleged commission of a criminal offence. As such, Bolt relies on substantial public interest / vital interests for such data sharing (s51 / s55(1)(iv) Irish Data protection Act) - processing here is proportionate, as only a limited account was shared.
** *Transparency*: The passenger privacy notice does not mention _proactively_ sharing info with the police - however, we can rely on “_we may also share your personal data with law enforcement or other public authorities, including … when the information is required by law or furthers a public interest task_.”

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Write to the rider explaining the situation.

We've received your request. Our team is working on two-week sprints. Your request would be evaluated based on legal deadlines and complexity and included in the relevant sprint.

Once we assess the sprint dates for your request (not later than 2 weeks from the request), the assignee would notify you in this ticket.

Please check 🌍 [User: Data requests|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/58951] to see if your request needs to be escalated to the Privacy Legal Team. If not, let us know in the ticket to cancel the request.

For urgent requests (legal deadline for responding to the user is shorter than 2 weeks), please tag Tatsiana Sivukha in this ticket.

Yes. Under Clause 4 (“Rental period, notice of termination”) the lease is locked-in for its first 12 months (1 Nov 2024 – 31 Oct 2025). Once that minimum term ends, it simply continues for an indefinite period and may be ended by either party on three months’ notice; there is no mechanism that rolls it into a new 12-month term. 

If you want to leave in January 2026, serve written notice no later than three months earlier to the potential moving date.

Recommendation 

# Document the landlord’s confirmation that the lease is rolling month-to-month after the first year. A short side letter or email acknowledgment referencing Clause 4 will eliminate any residual doubt.
# Diary the notice deadline now, and assign internal responsibility for sending the termination letter.

from legal POV:

If the warehouse contract ended in 2021 (so the deposit became due that same year), the claim to have the € 3 082 deposit repaid is now time-barred since 31 December 2024. German law gives only a three-year limitation period (§ 195 BGB), counted from the end of the calendar year in which the claim arose (§ 199 I BGB). 
If no legal action or Mahnverfahren was started before that date to suspend the clock (§ 204 I BGB), the landlord could now successfully plead _Verjährung_. (But we did ask for it, did we?)
Recovery prospects could therefore be minimal if we did not ask for the money to be paid by the landlord.

Under the Light Passenger Transport Services Regulations (S.L. 499.68), all ride-hailing drivers must meet specific criteria to be eligible for onboarding. The law sets out requirements for:

* Holding a valid driving license;
* Good conduct (including clean criminal and traffic record);
* Compliance with insurance and registration requirements.

The listed offences are mostly administrative traffic offences, but collectively they present significant public safety and compliance concerns. 

Therefore, I would not advise proceeding at least without official clearance from Transport Malta. Request confirmation that the driver's license and insurance are valid and that no disqualifications apply.

If Transport Malta clears the driver and their Jobsplus forms and license are valid, onboarding could be considered.

But without these preliminary measures we do not advise it. It is important to have in mind that granting platform access to a driver with this history without further verification may expose Bolt to reputational damages and issues with the regulatory authority.

Currently:
• We assign or close the search task if there’s no signal update within the threshold time.
• We mark a vehicle as “not available for order” if it doesn’t update its *location* within that same threshold.
This means that if a vehicle sends IoT updates with *invalid coordinates*, the system will close the search task, but the vehicle will remain in a “not available” state.
I’d appreciate your input here — what’s the best way to handle such vehicles? Should they be collected?

*a)* we shall clearly agree that the limit of liability of ours under the Suretyship Agreement shall not be increased under any circumstances;

*b)* our liability under the Suretyship Agreement shall be subsidiary and not primary, meaning that we shall only be obliged to satisfy Mobire’s  claims after Mobire has made all reasonable efforts to recover the obligations from Red Cab SIA directly, however without the need to initiate formal legal proceedings first. *c)* to limit our obligation to disclose certain business information of ours subject to it materially and adversely affect our ability to fulfill the obligations under the Suretyship Agreement;

*d)* we shall not be liable for claims arising from future agreements amending the Lease Contract between Red Cab SIA and Mobire, unless there is a written consent of ours on such amendments. We shall also clearly state that amendments to the Lease Contract between Red Cab SIA and Mobire or related agreements that would increase or alter our liability under the Suretyship Agreement shall not be binding on us unless expressly approved by us in writing in advance. As for now, theirs proposed draft agreement states the opposite.

For example, for *tetrapack bottles (12-pack)* priced at €13 per pack:

* Bolt would need to subsidize €7.50 for Bronze status
* €8.50 for Silver, Gold, and Platinum statuses

For *plastic bottles*, under the same logic:

* Bolt would subsidize €3.88 for Bronze
* €4.88 for the higher statuses

(Note: Option 2 is significantly more expensive than Option 1 because, in the first scenario, we work directly with a water producer, whereas in Option 2, we go through an intermediary — a promotional product supplier who partners with a water source. However, Option 2 allows us *not* to be the seller ourselves.)

{quote}_“Who would handle the bottle branding?”_{quote}

Branding would be handled by the water source affiliated with the promotional product company (under their supervision), after we provide the desired design (in compliance with our visual guidelines). The promotional product supplier would be accountable for the final result.

{quote}_“How would this be marketed to drivers?”_{quote}

The offer would be integrated into our official Bolt promotions (website/app). The partner (promotional supplier) would develop a dedicated platform where drivers could place their orders.
Simultaneously, the supplier would ship the water bottle pallets to our Saint-Ouen Hub.
We would organize scheduled pickup sessions (e.g. two per month) where driver partners could collect their pre-ordered packs.
They would book an appointment, be greeted by one of our agents, and receive their packs upon presentation of proof of purchase or invoice.

Please don’t hesitate to reach out with any further questions.

*Some of CapCut’s sounds can be used for commercial purposes on some platforms.*



CapCut has a library of copyright-free “Sounds for Commercial Use”.

* *Carefully filter for and select sounds specifically marked for “commercial use” within the CapCut library.*
* Sounds that are not explicitly marked for commercial use should be assumed to be for non-commercial use only.



However, even if a sound is marked for “commercial use”, that license is often only for use on TikTok or within the CapCut ecosystem (this is because both are owned by ByteDance).

*It is safe to post content with CapCut sounds marked for commercial use on CapCut, TikTok or TikTok for Business.*



*Using these sounds in ads on platforms like YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, or Google Ads can still put you at risk of copyright claims or violations*.



CapCut also offers a *Pippit AI paid plan*. This may be a better subscription option than Pro, as it is more legally sound and geared towards businesses.

The Pippit website states that "Most advertising content generated on Pippit AI is licensed for commercial use on TikTok and CapCut. *Some content is also licensed for commercial use on other platforms such as Facebook and Instagram*. Please click on each specific asset or template to see copyright information and license details." This means you should *check each sound individually to see what platforms it can be used on commercially.*

(Note that Pippit AI is also referred to as “CapCut for Business” or “CapCut Commerce Pro”.)



*_Side note_*_: CapCut’s Terms of Service states that users grant CapCut a broad, irrevocable, royalty-free, sublicencable, worldwide license to use their uploaded content (including voice, sounds, likeness, edits) for any purpose, commercial or otherwise, without requiring permission or paying them. This means that_ *_CapCut can use your content that you created with their tools commercially._*

* In order to identify the best timing to trigger the notification we checked the data for the last 5 months on the [+avg. trip duration+|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/rides/company_order?qid=jeqCh6qNQ2Q0QSsSg0zSSO&origin_space=6587&toggle=fil,vis]: {{14.4 min across markets.}}
* We’ve looked into the % of ride completion within 15 minutes from app launched per market by comparing it to the [+countrywise avg. ride duration+|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/rides/company_order?qid=mV3lIMNGyQ7Dc5M3c7tOdg&origin_space=6587&toggle=fil,vis] to identify the markets with the biggest drop-offs. We have several good candidates:
** *BE*: avg. trip duration is *13.9 min,* while % of ride completion within 15 min is *2.72%*
** *CZ*: avg. trip duration is *12.6* *min*, while % of ride completion within 15 min is *8.16%*
** *LV*: avg. trip duration is *12.8* *min*, while % of ride completion within 15 min is *5.47%*
** *ZA*: avg. trip duration is *11.9* *min*, while % of ride completion within 15 min is *10.24%*
** *ES*: avg. trip duration is *14.7* *min*, while % of ride completion within 15 min is *2.66%*
* Proposal is to run an experiment in these markets by triggering a notification to the TG if there is no Ride Finished event within 15 min from App Launched.
* Since we have no data indicating whether the ride might still be ongoing by the proposed threshold, we suggest keeping the copy quite generic, along the lines of: *_Have you secured your ride? Let us get you there - quick and easy._*
* Ideally, we should find a way to exclude the rides that might already be ongoing when the notification is triggered from the TG conversions, so as to not over-inflate results artificially with rides that would have happened regardless - e.g. rides finished within 1-2 minutes from when the notification gets triggered (although this shouldn't be a blocker for us to go ahead with the experiment)

h3. Analysis

* We encounter the error {{Got payment capture finished but there is no active booking}} when attempting to process a _refunded Payment Update Event_ for an inactive (cancelled) booking.
* Why are we receiving events for inactive bookings? Here’s the scenario:
** A user tries to book a ride using APM.
** The booking is successfully created, and payment is captured (since payment method is an APM).
** The user or vertical then cancels the existing booking and creates a new booking for the same amount.
** Although the existing booking is cancelled, it remains in an active state.
** When we receive this new booking request with identical parameters, the existing (cancelled) booking is marked as inactive [here|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/platform/commerce/balance_user/main/service/BookingService.ts#L280], and a new booking is created with the same parameters.
** Subsequently, we receive an undercapture refund payment update event for this old (cancelled)booking. Since this old booking is now inactive, we encounter the error {{Got payment capture finished but there is no active booking}}.
* What is the solution?
** Given that this is an expected scenario, we have downgraded the {{Got payment capture finished but there is no active booking}} log from error to a warning in Kibana.

+*Q.:*+ Regarding the data controller status — you mentioned that you are the data controller. Please justify this by specifying the legal basis under which you assume this role (e.g., legal obligation). Is there a legal act or an explanation from the State Data Protection Inspectorate on this matter? According to the provisions of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) 2016/679, EDPS guidelines, and considering the purpose — that you are acting in our interests and on our behalf as the data controller — we believe your status, in the context of our agreement, should be that of a data processor.

+*A.:*+ _As mentioned previously, please note that Bolt acts as an independent data controller when providing services to business customers. This role is clearly set out in Section 4 of the Bolt Business General Terms and Conditions (_[_link_|https://bolt.eu/lt-lt/legal/]_), which explicitly states that Bolt and the business customer act as separate and independent controllers with respect to their respective processing of personal data._

_Bolt determines the purposes and means of processing personal data required to operate the platform, manage user profiles, optimize transportation logistics, and ensure safety and compliance. In doing so, Bolt assumes full responsibility for its own processing operations and ensures full compliance with applicable data protection laws, including the GDPR._

_In support of this classification, Guidelines 07/2020 of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) on the concepts of controller and processor under the GDPR provide authoritative guidance. In particular, paragraph 82 and the "Example: Taxi Service" on page 27 illustrate a situation where a digital platform independently determines the processing of user data in connection with transport services. Although Bolt is a ride-hailing platform and not a taxi operator, the example provides useful analogical reasoning. IIt supports the conclusion that platforms which operate the digital infrastructure, determine user experience and data processing objectives, and contract directly with customers typically qualify as data controllers._

_Furthermore, as per Article 4(7) of the GDPR, a "controller" is the natural or legal person that “alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data.” Bolt determines why and how it processes personal data related to drivers and business accounts — from user registration, location tracking, fraud prevention, and invoicing — thus meeting the definition of a controller._

_To further demonstrate Bolt’s commitment to data protection, the company holds ISO/IEC 27001 certification, an internationally recognized standard for information security management. This reflects that Bolt not only assumes the role of a data controller in a formal sense but also implements a high level of operational and technical safeguards to protect personal data in accordance with Articles 24 and 32 GDPR (responsibility of the controller and security of processing)._

_In conclusion, both the contractual terms and the actual nature of Bolt’s data processing activities support the position that Bolt operates as an independent controller. This role is consistent with GDPR definitions, EDPB guidance, and applicable legal standards. Therefore, each party — Bolt and the business customer — remains independently responsible for their respective compliance obligations, including the provision of privacy notices, legal bases for processing, and the exercise of data subject rights._

h2. C2.5 overview

C2.5 batteries have been operating for a few months now. Batteries are distributed between 26 cities, with most of the batteries being in Warsaw (282 ASM, 1557 BSM), Riga (1839 ASM), Bucharest (1074 ASM).

!image-20250620-201711.png|width=605,height=374,alt="image-20250620-201711.png"!

Serial number explanation:

*ASM* - C2.2 - C2 Battery with "old" JingPin connector - *A*SM2501170001

*BSM* - C2.5 - C2 battery with "new" Higo connector - *B*SM2501170001

h3. *Status overview*

!image-20250620-201251.png|width=202,height=194,alt="image-20250620-201251.png"!

94% of C2.5 batteries are currently *operational*. 

353 pcs have been *sent to service*. Of these, 93% have an ASM serial number and use the JingPin connector. Feedback from Ilvestments indicates that most of the batteries have a broken female connector.

One thing to note is that Bucharest has sent 25% of their new batteries to repair. Keeping in mind that all their C2.5 batteries have the “old” connector, the % is still a lot higher than other cities. 

!image-20250620-201429.png|width=206,height=222,alt="image-20250620-201429.png"!

112 pcs are currently in *lost* state. 49 pcs are in *triaging*.

Thanks for the call yesterday! We now have a good plan to experiment Bolt Rewards monetary benefits.Summary of key decisions and actions, let me know if something is missing.

* Launch 50/50 AB experiment for Bolt Rewards Monetary Benefits in the beginning of August for all drivers in Stockholm (or did we agree for the whole Sweden?)
* Use Driver Rewards instead of Fleet Rewards. Exclude the ~10 fleets from the experiment who receive fleet deals at the moment.
* Other campaigns, mainly peak hour campaigns and branding bonuses will remain during the experiment. We accept that drivers have an opportunity to receive multiple benefits during the experiment. The AB test set-up will allow us to understand any incremental impact from the Bolt Rewards cash bonuses.
* The budget for the experiment comes from GA supply spend. The details of spend will be clarified during July. We’ll start with small spend, for example ~0.25% of GMV, to allow buffer to increase spend to reach 100% treatment, if test proves successful.
* Did we agree whether we’ll have cash bonus or commission kick-back? Based on previous GA campaigns experiments, there hasn’t been a significant difference between cash back and direct bonuses. UI needs to be adjusted accordingly before start of experiment [@rajat.kumar|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U04KS1JSRTP].

The issue is a miss match between tracking data timestamp and courier log states timestamp, causing in some cases lack of {{delivered}} state sent on the request to model invoker.

In [building|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d6a4cc5d1953376d8adc2e67286afc7aa30aaffd/src/delivery/geo/delivery_courier_tracking/main/service/OrderCourierRouteProcessor.ts#L167] the {{courier_route}} object that is sent to model invoker 2 sources are used: the tracking locations(from {{glue.geo__tracking_live.tracking_courier_locations_sqs}} via the {{v1CourierGetLocations}} API, the tracking location is sent every 2-3 seconds to backend) and {{courier_order_state_logs}} (from {{getOrderDataById}} API, keeps the state changes of an order).

* Both sources have timestamp and coordinates.
* The state of the order comes from {{courier_order_state_logs}}.
* All tracking data between the {{accepted}} state and the {{delivered}} state (according to the timestamps of {{courier_order_state_logs}}) is queried
* The 2 sources are then [combined|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d6a4cc5d1953376d8adc2e67286afc7aa30aaffd/src/delivery/geo/delivery_courier_tracking/main/service/OrderCourierRouteProcessor.ts#L167] to add state change information to tracking data
* Due to tracking data getting in every 2-3 seconds, there are cases when the {{delivered}} event is between 2 tracking records, causing it to be ignored and not added to the request to model invoker

The solution will be to include the {{delivered}} event with its own coordinates even though there is no corresponding {{tracking}} event at that timestamp.

Attached are the Kibana logs for the {{valid}} & {{invalid}} orders above. The [Kibana log|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d6a4cc5d1953376d8adc2e67286afc7aa30aaffd/src/delivery/geo/delivery_courier_tracking/main/service/OrderCourierRouteProcessor.ts#L151] has the first & last tracking data available (in the {{start}} and {{end}} fields) and the {{order_courier_state_logs}}.
It can be observed that for the {{valid}} order the last tracking data is at {{"server_time": 1748954668 //12:44:28}} and the {{delivered}} event is at {{"created": 1748954668, //12:44:28}} => the timestamps are equal, this [check|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d6a4cc5d1953376d8adc2e67286afc7aa30aaffd/src/delivery/geo/delivery_courier_tracking/main/service/OrderCourierRouteProcessor.ts#L179C33-L179C77] passes, the {{delivered}} event is included in the request.
For the {{invalid}} order the last tracking data is at {{"server_time": 1748954882 //12:48:02}} and the {{delivered}} is at {{"created": 1748954884, //12:48:04}}. There is no {{tracking}} data available at the {{delivered}} state so the event is not added to the request (I’ve check the table of tracking data, the next event is at {{2025-06-03 12:48:05.000}} but this one is not returned to backend because all tracking data between {{accepted}} and {{delivered}} is returned, this one is 1 second after {{delivered}}).

         , date_diff('day', t."start", t."end") as scheduled_duration
         , max(ss.min_duration)                 as required_duration
    from ng_public.targeting_test t
        inner join ng_public.targeting_primary_metric tpm
            on tpm.test_id = t.id
            and tpm.deleted = FALSE
        left join ng_public.targeting_sample_size ss
            on ss.test_id = tpm.test_id
            and ss.metric_key = tpm.metric_key
    where t.created_date between date '2023-09-01' and date_add('day', -1, now())
      and t.state not in ('ready_for_review', 'rejected', 'aborted', 'canceled')
    group by 1, 2, 3
    )
   , counts as (
    select created_month
         , count(t.test_id) as                                                                      num_tests
         , count_if(required_duration is not null)                                                  num_with_sample
         , count_if(required_duration <= 180)                                                       num_valid_sample
         , count_if(scheduled_duration >= required_duration)                                        num_sufficient_duration
         , count_if(scheduled_duration between 0.9 * required_duration and 1.2 * required_duration) num_optimal_duration
    from tests t
    group by created_month
    )
select created_month
     , 1.00 * num_sufficient_duration / num_valid_sample as share_sufficient_valid_duration
     , 1.00 * num_sufficient_duration / num_with_sample  as share_sufficient_duration
     , 1.00 * num_with_sample / num_tests                as share_with_sample
     , num_tests
     , num_with_sample
     , num_valid_sample
     , num_sufficient_duration
from counts
order by created_month asc;{code}

Hi [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad] , [~accountid:712020:8c797c70-7a57-496e-aa3f-5d91df806eb2] , I will answer the last question below.

*First*, based on recent jurisprudence from Constanța Court of Appeal, upheld by the High Court of Cassation and Justice, the legal interpretation of GEO 49/2019 is that only the main headquarters of the alternative transport operator qualifies for the issuance of transport authorizations. As such, I have serious doubts that the authorization claimed to have been obtained for Iași is valid under the current legal framework, unless the partner has established a main office there.

*Second*, Even if the fleet has 5 or more drivers working in Iași which under the Fiscal Code would trigger a local tax registration obligation, this aspect remains the fleet's responsibility, not Bolt’s. From our side, the key compliance checks are:

* That the fleet has a registered secondary +office in Iași+, and
* That it has obtained a +transport authorization i+n compliance with the law (which, again, is doubtful in this setup due to point 1 above).

In other words, Bolt’s obligation relates to ensuring that partners listed on the platform meet the legal conditions to perform alternative transport, not managing their fiscal reporting duties.

*Third*, from a labor law perspective, it is not illegal for all drivers to be employed under the Bucharest entity, as long as the employment contracts for those working in Iași explicitly +specify Iași as their place of work+. As such, from Bolt’s side, if the partner has registered this secondary office and appears to have obtained authorization (valid or not as per the recent jurisprudence), and if the drivers’ contracts reflect Iași as their work location, then providing this information to the Labour Authority should not be problematic, provided Bolt does not have knowledge that contradicts the legality of those operations. 

However, if Bolt is aware that the authorization was not validly issued for operations in Iași or is simply missing, then continuing to support the partner on the platform may expose Bolt to non-compliance risks, per GEO 49/2019, including fines of RON 5,000 to 15,000.

 

*Recommendations:*

* Request the legal position of the partner 's lawyer;

* Double check with ARR if the secondary office from Iasi is validly authorized;

* Internally, it is recommended to amend the [_Termenii generali aplicabili Operatorilor de Transport Alternativ_|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-driver/?category=rides][ (in force as of 24.02.2024)|https://bolt.eu/ro-ro/legal/tnc-driver/?category=rides], specifically Article 2.1.1, to explicitly require that the fleet holds +valid transport authorizations for all cities in which it operates.+ Additionally, the clause should clarify that +the fleet assumes full liability for any operations conducted without the necessary transport authorizations, and/or in breach of labour or fiscal obligations+, where services are provided by employees.

Please let me know your thoughts on the above.

📊  *A/B Test Result – Driver Radius Adjustment (Gothenburg, Q2 2025)*
We’ve completed the evaluation of the driver radius A/B test in Gothenburg, where we tested a 1km default radius against the existing setup. Here’s a quick summary of the findings:

🔍 *Key Results:*

* *Treatment EPH:* €32.54
* *Control EPH:* €35.32
* *Observed EPH difference:* −€2.78/hr
* *p-value:* 0.017 → Statistically significant
* *CI:* [−€5.07, −€0.49]

(/)  While statistically significant, this difference reflects lower EPH for the treatment group.

📉 *However, after adjusting for pre-test performance:*

* *Treatment EPH change:* +€0.22
* *Control EPH change:* +€1.81
* *Difference-in-Differences (DiD):* −€1.59

This suggests that Control improved more than Treatment, and the radius change did not lead to better earnings.

📈 *One positive signal:*
The *Treatment group saw higher improvement in partner acceptance rate* compared to Control, indicating that a tighter radius may surface more relevant orders to drivers.

⚠️ *Important note – possible interference across groups:*
Since Control drivers (with 2km+ radius) were eligible for more orders, they may have taken requests that would have otherwise gone to Treatment drivers. This kind of cross-group interaction can distort test results, especially when testing dispatch-related features.
💡 *What this means:*
The 1km radius might still be beneficial, but it needs to be tested in an environment where all drivers use the same radius logic (e.g. a full-market test).

📌  *Recommendation:*
*Do not expand the 1km default radius based on this test alone.*
Instead:

* Revert the change for affected fleets (done (/) )
* Consider a market-wide test to properly evaluate impact in a unified setting

* *Problem 1: Do we need a DSA or other agreement?*
** *Drivers*: No, we don't need a formal DSA between drivers and Bolt to enable this feature. But we do need to inform referred drivers clearly and early in the journey that their data will be shared with the person who referred them if they input a referral code. A disclaimer in-app (directly below the referral code field) could be the right approach. 
** *Scouts*: We already have a DSA for them, which is fine. Easiest solution: include a short in-app notice and require a click-through/checkbox the first time they access the enhanced referral section. 
** From a privacy POV, I do not see that an agreement between a scout and a driver who is referred would be needed to facilitate the data sharing; what is important to us is that the Scout holds the responsibility on collecting the data and sharing it with us in a compliant way - we can do that by adding a disclaimer “I confirm that I have the right to submit data of the referred person” or something similar. We can check in with Merve in Slack if any Terms are needed from a legal POV.
* *Problem 2: Signed-up driver doesn’t know their data is shared*
** Agreed: show a clear, short disclaimer under the referral code field during sign-up. That’s the most legally defensible and frictionless point of notice. 
* *Problem 3: Scope of data shared*
** Aligned - no further comments. 
* *Problem 4: Duration of data visibility*
** “removing the phone number and number of trips so the referee will only see the first name to know who completed or expired” → in principle, this works, but perhaps I could see the design later to understand if there’s any issues?

Hi [~accountid:5b7beb46b8624857f09efff9] : 

* *Do we need driver consent to show dashcam notifications to riders?*
** No, not for this pilot. These are driver-installed dashcams, and Bolt isn’t processing the footage. However, it's worth letting drivers know we’re testing this so they’re not caught off guard by rider questions. A one-time in-app heads-up or support message is enough.
* *Timing and tone of rider notification*
** 🟠 Risk: showing the notification _after_ booking and warning of longer ETAs may make riders feel pressured to accept a ride they're uncomfortable with.
** Suggested quick fix:
*** Move the CCTV notification earlier in the rider journey (ideally before final confirmation).
*** Soften the language: e.g., “Some drivers use dashcams for safety. You can cancel if you prefer not to be recorded.” or ““This ride may be recorded with a dashcam for safety. Cancel if you prefer not to be recorded - availability may vary.”
** *Is there a precedent we can follow?*
*** Uber allows drivers to register dashcams, and riders are notified _during checkout_, before confirming. Riders can cancel without penalty within a grace period (usually 2 minutes). Worth mirroring.

*_Some questions:_*

* Will we only show the notifications to riders if they order a trip with one of these 22 drivers or all drivers?
* How long do we want to run this for? I suggest this to be limited in time.
* Will we be preparing any sort of a short FAQ or support link explaining why some drivers record (e.g., for safety)?
* Will this experiment collect any metrics tied to cancellations or complaints?

Also see this for some examples of regulatory expectations/best practices: [https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/FPF-Uber-DashcamResourceforDrivers-Mobile-Proposed-Final.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com|https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/FPF-Uber-DashcamResourceforDrivers-Mobile-Proposed-Final.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

[~accountid:712020:634c40ac-eff2-4487-aaa9-f38b92a7bf83] from an EU VAT (as we mention EE, LT, LV, RO, CZ, PT.)   the only relevant articles are from *EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC*



* Article 78(b): States that the taxable amount _shall not include price reductions by way of discounts or rebates allowed to the customer and accounted for at the time of the supply._
* Article 90(1): Allows for a reduction in the taxable amount where discounts or rebates are granted _after_ the supply has been made.

AS the discount is agreed and applied _before time of sale_:

* Show the *full price*, then list the *discount* (either as a line item or included in the unit price).
* VAT is calculated *on the net amount* (price after discount).
* Invoice must include:
** Gross amount
** Discount (as percentage or fixed amount)
** Net amount
** VAT rate and total VAT
** Total amount payable 

h3. 

Discount After the Supply (Credit Note) If a discount is granted after the invoice is issued, but this is not the case.



When the discount is equal or bigger then the transaction: i.e. our commission netting with incentives sometimes in RH it’s not disciplined by the directive but in practice:

Companies  often issue a *"zero invoice"* in order to:

* Record the transaction, Show the discount to the customer, also for audit trails or internal controls.

Such an invoice typically states:

* Original value of the supply,
* Full discount applied,
* Resulting VAT is *€0*,
* Total payable is *€0*.

I think is what we do in practice  but if we want to overcome the issue of rejection of an invoice from the real-time systems like in RO some companies charge like 0.10€ just to make it accepted, should we do this trick?

Effectively, the benefits of membership in the cooperative include being able to participate in large tenders and contracted work that are won / negotiated by the COOP on behalf of drivers, as well as being able to make use of COOP vehicles if needed, and access to spare parts at a reduced rate.

With respect to the earnings that drivers generate, take the following as an example:
If a fare on Bolt is 100 EUR;

- Bolt will receive 20 EUR as commission (20%)
- VAT on the ride will be 18 EUR (18%)
- The remaining 62 EUR will be earned by the driver for completing the trip (62%)

COOP will then take a 5% cut of the total net earnings of the drivers. So effectively it is a profit-sharing agreement, very heavily weighted in favour of the driver.

In the meantime, please allow me to reiterate the advice that was given by external counsel when the legal analysis of the Branded Car program was launched: 


* *Reclassification Risk*: The program carries a non-negligible risk (up to 30%) of drivers being reclassified as employees due to financial incentives tied to ride activity, control mechanisms (e.g., monthly sticker checks), and the exclusivity of branding. However, this risk can be reduced to around 10% by implementing *key mitigation strategies* such as *allowing multi-branding*, *paying for advertising* +*independently*+ *of ride activity*, and *ensuring that contracts are clearly framed as advertising agreements* rather than employment relationships.

* *Advertising Structure*: Drivers should act as media owners selling ad space. Contracts must clearly reflect this to avoid employment requalification.

* *Contractual Imbalance*: Variable pay models may breach Art. L.442-6 (Code de commerce). Use fixed + retro pay, allow opt-out and sticker removal.

*3. Invoicing & VAT Treatment*

* Advertising services are subject to standard VAT (20%), which is different from the reduced rate applicable to passenger transport (10%). 
* VAT-compliant invoices should be applied - this may require a Tax implications to confirm this.

Hi [~accountid:712020:0699af2f-6b23-4d6c-8001-b28978cbddc5], this is a +*high-risk request*+ because all three initiatives could be regarded as additional incentives based on driver performance and participation in the Branded Program ❗ 

*1. “10k Event” - Surprise 5,000€ Prize*

* When organising a giveaway, it is important, to have gambling considerations in mind so as to not fall under that regime which requires a specific license from the Autorité Nationale des Jeux (ANJ). According to Article L. 320-1 of the French Internal Security Code, +a game is considered gambling if it involves+:
*# A public offer to participate;
*# A stake or financial consideration by participants *_[the requirement to get a sticker affixed to their car could be argued as asking for a stake from the participants]_*;
*# The hope of winning a prize (usually of monetary value);
*# Outcome determined predominantly by chance.
* Article L121-36 of the French Consumer Code requires T&Cs to be drafted and made public to the participants. Failure to do so can create legal exposure for misleading commercial practices. 
* What is the rationale to offer 5,000€ ? The higher the amount, the higher the exposure to risk. 
* The participation to the chance based giveaway is linked to affixing the branded sticker, there is the first risk that the amount will be considered payment linked to the advertising service and not a payment as part of a unrelated giveaway. 
* If the amount is not inexchange for the advertising services, and is purely a promotional prize, then no VAT is due from the driver, however Bolt may still be liable to account for VAT (Tax should be looped in to confirm).
* If the driver is renting a car from a fleet owner, who should get the amount ? 


→ Considering the risk of it being perceived as gambling y the ANJ, the risk of reclass if perceived as additional incentive for services and the considerable amount being offered, I would not recommend going forward with this initiative. If the objective is to boost leads, I would suggest we discuss a different approach with a giveaway that is less risky.


*2. Branded Cars with Goodie Bags*

* This could increase the reclassification risk, especially if the goodie bags include equipment (dashcams, chargers) that could be used during Bolt rides, this could strengthen the appearance of an employer-employee relationship.
* What would be the narrative around this campaign? Would it be promoted as a promotional campaign?



*3. 5,000€ Lottery*

* Drivers should not be automatically enrolled to a giveaway (to avoid any ambiguity with the FR term of lottery which is most commonly used as gambling is english, please refer to this as a giveaway), as this includes processing of personal data; consent should be explicitly required.
* What is implied by the Bolt Wallet? Is this money that the driver can withdraw at any time? How can they use this amount?
* If you wish to have a pure giveaway, can the prize be something else than a monetary prize? In collaboration with the marketing team, a promotional code by a partner might be more appropriate and would remove some of the risk.
* T&Cs should be drafted and published for this chance-based giveaway campaign.



Kindly could you share some additional context to each ? Happy to schedule a call to go through potential solutions to organise giveaways to boost leads which are less risky than those suggested above. 

Thank you

There are a couple of things I think we need to figure out, in order of priority.

h2. Converging workflows and reusing results

h3. Identify the longest jobs and steps in these jobs

* Can we speed up or eliminate the longest steps by reusing some artefacts from the previous job in the same workflow?
* Which workflows can we merge to maximise the benefits of reusing artefacts? Can we have a single “CI workflow” and a single “Deploy workflow” for the changed projects?

h3. How to share the artefacts?

h4. Docker image

* There are some ways to pass the Docker image between the jobs [https://docs.docker.com/build/ci/github-actions/share-image-jobs/|https://docs.docker.com/build/ci/github-actions/share-image-jobs/]
* Publishing to the registry takes time.
* If we run single-machine, self-hosted runners, there’s no need to publish the image. I don’t think it will be possible with K8S runners.
* The image can be converted to a tarball and passed through GitHub artefacts. However, we end up using GitHub Artifacts.
* A nice bonus of having a CI image for the project is that it can be reproduced or pulled locally, if debugging is needed. But it’s just a bonus.

h4. GitHub Artifacts 

* [https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/storing-and-sharing-data-from-a-workflow|https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/storing-and-sharing-data-from-a-workflow]
* We have reusable actions that upload results into GitHub Artifacts, like
** dbt-parse [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/.github/actions/dbt-parse/action.yml|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/.github/actions/dbt-parse/action.yml], which uploads the target directory. 
** Fetching prod manifest [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/.github/actions/fetch-production-manifest/action.yml|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/.github/actions/fetch-production-manifest/action.yml]

h2. dbt artefacts

h3. Per-project artefacts

* On each deploy, for each project, we run dbt docs to generate manifest, semantic manifest, and catalog files [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171/job/44676675502#step:6:1|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171/job/44676675502#step:6:1]
* They are uploaded to the {{s3://bolt-data-modelling-platform}} in this step [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171/job/44676675502#step:9:13|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171/job/44676675502#step:9:13] 
* The manifest is used in the Jobs when defer is used, so it has to be published as soon as possible and reflect the current state of the project.
* The question is - do we need the catalog.json for each project? It takes the longest to generate and maybe we don’t even need it.

h3. Global project artefacts

* They contain information about all resources in all projects.
* It takes a long time to complete - usually around 30 minutes.
* It is used for:
** DataHub ingestion. We haven’t seen the benefits of separate ingestion of dbt projects so far.
** The dbt-docs page, although we’re going to kill it once everyone is happy with DataHub. These are published in the project release workflow, regardless of changed projects [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171/job/44676675508#step:6:11|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171/job/44676675508#step:6:11]
** Local runs with defer because users don’t have access to the bolt-data-modelling-platform bucket - they download the prod manifest using the dbt-docs domain as a proxy to S3.
** Upload to Euno, which requires both manifest and catalog [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/workflows/upload_to_euno.yml|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/workflows/upload_to_euno.yml]
** Building project evaluation [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/workflows/build_project_evaluation.yml|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/workflows/build_project_evaluation.yml]
* So it is still needed, but maybe we don’t have to do it immediately after the merge? 

h3. Idea: maybe we don’t have to build full catalog on each merge? 

* When several PRs are merged within one hour, at most 2 runs of that job would complete. So, by the time they complete, the manifest is already out of date when compared to the main branch.
* Known use cases for the catalog don’t require it to be as close as possible to the current state of the main branch.
* *Could we build it every 1, 2, or 3 hours unless there are cases that wouldn’t accept the delay?*
* It would reduce the inflated release workflow time
** The majority of the Project changes release workflow [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683171] that runs on each push to main is full catalog generation for the global project. 
** It gives a false impression that it’s how long it takes for changes to be available in production.
** If we decide we don’t need a per-project catalog, we can significantly reduce the release workflow time.
* It would also free up worker slots.

h2. Bundle deployment

* We can speed it up slightly by reusing some artefacts but it’s the bundle deploy command that takes the longet.
* We have to understand what the slowest part of bundle deployment is.
* It can take ~15 minutes [https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683185/job/44676678970#step:11:13|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/actions/runs/15848683185/job/44676678970#step:11:13]
* Can we speed up the upload of the dbt project to the Databricks Workspace files?
* If we can’t speed it up, should we change our deployment strategy so that the dbt project code is not part of the bundle?

h3. Alternative deployment strategy

* *This is out of scope now, but noting for future reference.*
* That would require a different mechanism for making the dbt project’s code available for the Databricks Jobs.
* We included all of the dbt projects’ code in the Docker image that’s used for sensors and SQL Warehouses.
** Downside: a change in one project, like the common project, could break other projects.
** However, if projects code goes out of sync, we get into this problem [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/INS-761|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/INS-761]
** We’ll have to decide which of these causes less harm.

We will decide whether to continue using the k8s runners based on the redesigned structure of GitHub workflows.

The biggest factors that we know of now:

* How many jobs will we run once we reorganise?
* What state and how should be passed between the jobs within the workflow?
* Do we need to control the runner image? Can we install the required dependencies that don’t change in the startup scripts? Can we efficiently cache more dynamic dependencies?

Infrastructure options that we have:

* GitHub-hosted runners. These could still be used for the simplest possible actions that don’t require special dependencies or connection to our internal systems.
* [SRE-hosted runners|https://github.com/bolteu/terraform-main/tree/4dc5d5dccf75354b81b215558ae98d511364fa11/_modules/github-runner], which we’ve used in the past. No autoscaling, less control over the image (but maybe we don’t need it?).
* Kubernetes runners, but with [autoscaling|https://docs.github.com/en/actions/hosting-your-own-runners/managing-self-hosted-runners-with-actions-runner-controller/deploying-runner-scale-sets-with-actions-runner-controller#setting-the-maximum-and-minimum-number-of-runners] - we’re running on a static number of workers now.

Moje mišljenje je da je Grad Dubrovnik uveo promjenu čije posljedice nije u potpunosti predvidio, niti se na njih logistički i pravovremeno pripremio. Iako gradonačelnik u medijskim istupima kontinuirano ističe kako ima podršku i suradnju s aplikacijama, što je točno u okviru onoga da smo mi voljni surađivati u područjima gdje možemo, odnosno što je u našoj moći, ali je važno naglasiti nekoliko izazova. Naime, prema mojim saznanjima, još uvijek nemamo službeni popis svih vozila koja posjeduju propusnice, niti je poznato kada ćemo te podatke zaprimiti od Grada. Samim time, nismo u mogućnosti procijeniti kojom brzinom ćemo se moći organizirati, kao ni koliki će opseg posla biti potreban, osobito uzimajući u obzir da uskoro započinje razdoblje godišnjih odmora. Nadalje, prema mojim saznanjima imamo stvarna ograničenja u provedbi, odnosno još nismo u mogućnosti integrirati rute zabrana i dodjeljivanja vožnji unutar aplikacije.  

Sporne točke: 

* “_Grad Dubrovnik će XY dostaviti podatke o registarskoj oznaci vozila za vozila s reguliranim statusom iz stavka 2. ovog članka_.” - *nije naveden datum do kada će Grad dostaviti podatke.* 



* “_Grad Dubrovnik će obavijestiti XY u slučaju da vozilo s reguliranim statusom, iz stavka 2. ovog članka, prestane ostvarivati pravo ili izgubi pravo na ulaz, prometovanje i izlaz iz Užeg središta Grada Dubrovnika tijekom primjene Prometnog sustava te se XY obvezuje u tom slučaju ažurirati svoje Podatke._” - *nije naveden rok u kojem će Grad javljati ukoliko je neko vozilo izgubilo propusnicu.* 



* “_XY će poduzeti sve potrebne mjere kako bi omogućio i osigurao da samo vozila s reguliranim statusom iz stavka 2. ovog članka mogu pružati uslugu autotaksi prijevoza na način da se narudžba prijevoza realizira elektroničkom Aplikacijom._” - *Ukoliko nismo tehnički u mogućnosti unutar aplikacije osigurati da se vožnje u Zonu zabrane ulaska dodjeljuju isključivo vozilima s važećom propusnicom, moj je prijedlog/mišljenje da ne potpisujemo MoU. Naime, u slučaju da dođe do prekršaja (doći će jer dolazi i sada), postoji realna sumnja da će Grad, nakon potpisivanja dokumenta, a kako bi zaštitio vlastiti ugled u javnosti, odgovornost za sve eventualne propuste i pogreške u rutiranju prebaciti na aplikacije. Osim toga, time bismo doveli u pitanje i imidž naše tvrtke, budući da bismo svjesno potpisali dokument za čije tehničko provođenje trenutno nismo spremni. Time bi naša riječ i potpis izgubili vjerodostojnost, a Gradu bismo zapravo dali prostor da nas javno prozove i pozicionira kao uzrok problema.*



Pitala sam ChatGPT što se događa u slučaju kada jedna strana ne može ispuniti obveze iz MoU-a zbog tehničkih razloga, na što sam dobila odgovor da takvi razlozi ne predstavljaju višu silu i stoga nisu opravdanje za nepoštovanje dogovora. U tom slučaju, druga ugovorna strana može tražiti naknadu štete. Iako je zaista malo vjerojatno da će Grad Dubrovnik pokretati pravni postupak, važno je istaknuti da ih potpisani MoU na određeni način štiti – jer omogućuje da se odgovornost za kaotičnu provedbu mjera prebaci na platforme. Drugim riječima, takav dokument Gradu može poslužiti kao argument da su aplikacije bile suglasne s provedbom, čime potencijalni problemi više nisu njihova odgovornost.

h1. UPDATE (24.06)

+*BACKGROUND*+

* On 3 April 2025, a Norwegian rider ([profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/82375578/overview]) wrote to Bolt via in-app message ([link|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/548855359]) noting unrecognised trips on their account (provided screenshots). Rider wanted compensation.
** CS flagged to the rider that the trips were taken by someone called ‘Oskar’, who had changed the name on the account (rider does not recognise this name). Various trips taken on the account, which match the screenshots provided by the rider - this suggests account itself compromised.
** Total financial detriment apparently comes to around 3624 NOK (£282). Rider has confirmed that the card has been blocked.
* On the same day, CS logged all devices out of the account. Rider then logged back in. 
** Nothing to suggest any other active devices on the account since then. As such, incident does not appear to be ongoing.
* Rider has demanded: (i) compensation; and (ii) an explanation of what happened and threatened to go to the media.
** On 17 April, CS asked user if they had been at pickup area on the relevant date, as well as whether they received SMS messages. User responded “_No, I have not been. Unfortunately, I don't have access to the email_ [_ingridvif@gmail.com_|mailto:ingridvif@gmail.com] _either, it's linked to my Facebook_”.
** No further messages since 28 April.
* Based on internal investigation:
** On 1 April, name change to Oskar Hag (since reverted). No other account detail changes.
** Based on message thread, the rider still uses the phone number on the account. This suggests this is not a case of phone number recycling.
** Name change to Oskar came from device A8CF1336-BA7C-42B6-8F77-77E1B4D89268. That is the one different device in the login history (iPhone 15,3), which logged in via ‘phone’ method. This was deactivated on 3 April.
** Auth team confirmed: “_What is suspicious is that both fraudulent device id_ {{A8CF1336-BA7C-42B6-8F77-77E1B4D89268}} _and the old device id (_{{A12B9E3A-F656-4771-9754-98D8AA46C8DF}}_) have orders with same pickup (_{{Rastaveien 12D, Lørenskog 1461, Oslo, Norway}}_). Same address was used as destination in the past as well. We believe that the account was not actually stolen, but the user is just trying to scam us._” CS confirmed “_This is the explanation with highest probability, any other explanation (like account really being hijacked) we couldn't find proof._” ([LINK|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C06R63EQ6CS/p1745313819679069?thread_ts=1744053914.254599&cid=C06R63EQ6CS])

+*ANALYSIS*+

* The bottom line for this case is that the auth team have now concluded that it is more likely that the user is trying to scam us than it is the account was compromised. As such, we do not have enough information to be confident that a data breach actually occurred here.

*Issue:* 

*The way modals are built in Admin does work well with the process.*

* Using the same targeting setup would not let the same user see the modal again if they’ve already seen it the allowed number of times. 
** The ‘Not seen more than X times’ rule counts the modal ID, not the Targeting ID.
** To solve this, we need to clone the modal itself so that a new modal ID is created. 

*But this creates another issue:*

* Cloning the modal would mean all localisations are lost in Crowdin since the modal ID is different.



*Solutions*:

# Creating localised versions of the modal in Admin so translations do not come from Crowdin:
## +E.g., Bad Weather - en 🇬🇧+ + +Bad Weather - lt 🇱🇹+
## This means there will need to be 2 Modal Poll Targetings that check for the user’s language and only display the modal if it matches to this.
# We give local ops access to CrowdIn and teach them how to use it:
## Not the best option as this also gives them access to every other modal that exists.
# We give them a shorter delivery time if one of these templates needs to be used. E.g. 2 hours.

Hey, [~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] - I am covering for Kostya in the analysis of the swipe mechanism. The current proposal (see below), imo, does not meet the required standards. I have prepared my proposal below. Would you like to confirm whether it is the correct way of thinking? 

~ Analysis of the Swipe Data mechanism ~

# *Legal framework at a glance*

* Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019).
* PDPC “Guideline on Requesting Consent” (7 September 2022): soft-law guidance.

# *Statutory consent requirements (PDPA § 19)*

Consent must be written/electronic, freely given, specific, informed, obtained before any collection, and revocable through the same channel at no cost.

# *PDPC Consent Guideline – practical expectations*

* State one concrete purpose, not a broad catch-all.
* Visually and functionally separate the consent box from other notices or contractual terms.
* Use plain language in Thai (and any other relevant language).
* Obtain a clear affirmative act that cannot be misinterpreted (examples: ticking a box, clicking a button, etc.).

# Does the current version satisfy these rules?

* *It seems that the currently proposed format does not meet the expected criteria.* 
* Alone “Claim” button is not enough for valid PDPA consent (it does not specify what data, the word “claim” could easily be misread as per the purpose of sharing. The user must clearly understand that tapping it authorises Bolt to share specific data with Igloo for a stated purpose and that they can withdraw consent just as easily.

!Screenshot_20250520_104032_Bolt Driver (2) (f3c9e32a-158a-4777-86e7-30126a03162e).jpg|width=16.666666666666664%!

# *Proposal*

Alone “Claim” button is not enough for valid PDPA consent. The user must clearly understand that tapping it authorises Bolt to share specific data with Igloo for a stated purpose and that they can withdraw consent just as easily.

*Minimum fixes to reach compliance:*

* Add a consent statement directly above the button, e.g. “_By tapping ‘Agree & Claim’, you consent to Bolt sharing your [specify the exact categories of personal data] with Igloo for the purpose of sending you a motor insurance offer._”
* Change the button text so the consent meaning is unmistakable (e.g. “_Agree & Claim_”).
* Link to a Thai-language privacy notice, using a wording “_See the Privacy Notice here._”
* The whole screen should be in Thai.

[~accountid:712020:020c4e37-f90b-4930-8f57-98a6bca82856], siunčiu perverstą.

*Klausimas:* Dėl duomenų valdytojo statuso – Jūs minėjote, kad esate duomenų valdytojas. Prašome pagrįsti tai, nurodant teisinį pagrindą, kuriuo remiantis prisiimate šį vaidmenį (pvz., teisinė prievolė). Ar yra kokio nors teisės akto ar Valstybinės duomenų apsaugos inspekcijos išaiškinimo šiuo klausimu? Atsižvelgiant į Bendrojo duomenų apsaugos reglamento (BDAR) 2016/679 nuostatas, EDPS gaires bei į tai, kad veikiate mūsų interesais ir mūsų vardu kaip duomenų valdytojas, manome, jog pagal mūsų susitarimą Jūsų statusas turėtų būti duomenų tvarkytojo.

*Atsakymas:* Kaip jau buvo minėta, atkreipiame dėmesį, kad „Bolt“ teikia paslaugas verslo klientams kaip nepriklausomas duomenų valdytojas. Šis vaidmuo aiškiai nurodytas „Bolt Business“ bendrosiose sąlygose, 4 skyriuje ([*nuoroda*|https://bolt.eu/lt-lt/legal/]), kur tiesiogiai pažymėta, kad „Bolt“ ir verslo klientas veikia kaip atskiri ir nepriklausomi duomenų valdytojai kiekvienas savo duomenų tvarkymo atžvilgiu.

„Bolt“ pats nustato asmens duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir priemones, reikalingas platformos veikimui, naudotojų paskyrų valdymui, transporto logistikos optimizavimui bei saugumo ir teisinių reikalavimų užtikrinimui. Tokiu būdu „Bolt“ visiškai atsako už savo duomenų tvarkymo veiksmus ir užtikrina atitiktį taikomiems duomenų apsaugos teisės aktams, įskaitant BDAR.

Šiam klasifikavimui pagrįsti remiamasi Europos duomenų apsaugos valdybos (EDPB) Gairėmis 07/2020 dėl duomenų valdytojo ir tvarkytojo sąvokų pagal BDAR. Ypač svarbus 82 punktas ir pavyzdys „Taksi paslaugos“ (27 psl.), kuriame aprašyta situacija, kai skaitmeninė platforma pati nustato duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir priemones transporto paslaugų kontekste. Nors „Bolt“ nėra taksi operatorius, šis pavyzdys analogiškai pagrindžia išvadą, kad platformos, kurios valdo skaitmeninę infrastruktūrą, formuoja naudotojo patirtį, nustato duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir sudaro sutartis su klientais, paprastai laikomos duomenų valdytojais.

Be to, pagal BDAR 4 straipsnio 7 dalį, „duomenų valdytojas“ – tai fizinis ar juridinis asmuo, kuris „vienas arba kartu su kitais nustato asmens duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir priemones“. „Bolt“ apibrėžia, kodėl ir kaip yra tvarkomi asmens duomenys, susiję su vairuotojais ir verslo paskyromis – nuo naudotojo registracijos, buvimo vietos sekimo, sukčiavimo prevencijos iki sąskaitų išrašymo – ir taip atitinka duomenų valdytojo apibrėžimą.

Siekdamas dar labiau pagrįsti savo įsipareigojimus duomenų apsaugai, „Bolt“ yra sertifikuotas pagal ISO/IEC 27001 – tarptautinį informacijos saugumo valdymo standartą. Tai rodo, kad „Bolt“ ne tik formaliai prisiima duomenų valdytojo vaidmenį, bet ir įgyvendina aukšto lygio technines bei organizacines priemones, saugančias asmens duomenis, kaip reikalaujama pagal BDAR 24 ir 32 straipsnius (duomenų valdytojo atsakomybė ir saugumas).

Apibendrinant, tiek sutartinės sąlygos, tiek faktinė „Bolt“ duomenų tvarkymo veikla pagrindžia, kad „Bolt“ veikia kaip nepriklausomas duomenų valdytojas. Toks statusas atitinka BDAR apibrėžimus, EDPB gaires ir taikytinus teisės aktus. Todėl abi šalys – „Bolt“ ir verslo klientas – lieka savarankiškai atsakingos už atitiktį, įskaitant privatumo pranešimų pateikimą, teisėto tvarkymo pagrindo nustatymą ir duomenų subjektų teisių įgyvendinimą.

*Klausimas:* Kokie mūsų darbuotojų asmens duomenys bus naudojami platformoje (vardas, pavardė, telefono numeris, kelionės vieta ir kt.)?

*Atsakymas:* Jūsų darbuotojai turės pateikti tik telefono numerį (jis yra privalomas ir turi būti teisingas). Jokia kita asmeninė informacija nebus prašoma. Taip pat bus renkami kelionės duomenys: paėmimo vieta, laikas, kelionės atstumas ir pan.

*Klausimas:* Ar automobilyje bus vykdoma vaizdo ar garso įrašų registracija?

*Atsakymas:* Pagal mūsų vairuotojų bendrųjų sąlygų 4.3 punktą, vairuotojams aiškiai draudžiama be leidimo daryti vaizdo ar garso įrašus teikiant pavėžėjimo paslaugas. Konkretūs draudimai:

* filmuoti ar transliuoti vaizdo įrašus internete be leidimo;
* daryti garso įrašus automobilyje;
* fotografuoti ar filmuoti keleivius be išankstinio informuoto sutikimo.

Šie ribojimai įtvirtinti keleivių privatumo apsaugai ir laikantis taikytinų duomenų apsaugos įstatymų, įskaitant BDAR.

*Klausimas:* Ar 2 klausime minėti duomenys bus perduodami Jūsų pasirinktiems duomenų tvarkytojams, subduomenų tvarkytojams ar trečiosioms šalims?

*Atsakymas:* Atkreipiame dėmesį, kad „Bolt“ veikia tarptautiniu mastu, todėl asmens duomenys gali būti perduoti, saugomi ir (arba) tvarkomi „Bolt Group“ įmonių, subrangovų ar partnerių, vykdant sutartinius įsipareigojimus už šalies, kurioje yra klientas, ribų. Išsamią informaciją apie trečiąsias šalis ir šalis, į kurias gali būti perduodami duomenys, rasite čia: _Bolt Group Companies and Controllers lists_.

*Klausimas:* Ar duomenys bus perduodami už ES ribų?

*Atsakymas:* Kadangi „Bolt“ veikia tarptautiniu mastu, asmens duomenys gali būti perduodami, saugomi ir tvarkomi „Bolt Group“ įmonių, subrangovų ar partnerių, vykdant sutartinius įsipareigojimus už kliento šalies ribų. Išsamią informaciją apie šalis, į kurias gali būti perduodami duomenys, rasite čia: _Bolt Group Companies and Controllers lists_.

Perduodant asmens duomenis už ES ar EEE ribų, „Bolt“ imasi visų būtinų veiksmų laikytis teisinių reikalavimų, taiko atitinkamus duomenų perdavimo mechanizmus: *tinkamumo sprendimus* ir *standartines sutarčių sąlygas (SCCs)*.

*Klausimas:* Kur yra duomenų centrai, kuriuose saugoma platformos informacija?

*Atsakymas:* Švedijoje, Airijoje ir Vokietijoje.

Hvala [~accountid:712020:b082e95c-63c0-4004-9087-5d679b83872b] na temeljitom pregledu ugovora. 

[~accountid:63314e9e9b32cfef93265252] Iako dokument nosi naziv „Sporazum o razumijevanju“, njegov sadržaj pokazuje da se radi *o pravno obvezujućem ugovoru*, a ne o neformalnom ili neobvezujućem Sporazumu (MoU).

Sporazum se odnosi isključivo na razmjenu podataka između Grada Dubrovnika i Bolta. Konkretno, Grad će Boltu dostavljati informacije o taksi vozilima koja imaju pravo ulaska u posebno reguliranu zonu unutar povijesne jezgre (tzv. Uže središte), a Bolt se obvezuje iskljucivo:

# Ažurirati podatke u aplikaciji čim Grad javi da neko vozilo više nema pravo pristupa toj zoni.
# Omogućiti da narudžbe za vožnje u toj zoni mogu prihvaćati isključivo vozila koja imaju „regulirani status“.
# Redovno i aktivno obavještavati vozače o pravilima prometovanja u toj zoni.

Ugovor nije detaljan i ostavlja značajan prostor za tumačenje. Ipak, smatram da Bolt nije izložen financijskoj odgovornosti – Grad ne bi mogao izreći novčane kazne Boltu ako njegovi vozači krše pravila, niti bi mogao zabraniti svim vozačima Bolta ulazak u određeno područje isključivo zato što koriste Boltovu platformu.

Bolt djeluje isključivo kao posrednik i pružatelj aplikacije te nije nositelj licence za pružanje usluga prijevoza.

Ako Bolt prekrši ugovor, jedini realan rizik je da Grad odluči raskinuti ugovor i prestane dijeliti podatke – što u svakom slučaju može učiniti i bez povrede ugovora, uz otkazni rok od 15 dana. Teoretski postoji mogućnost da Grad pokuša tužiti Bolt za naknadu štete, no to smatram vrlo malo vjerojatnim. Grad bi morao dokazati da je pretrpio stvarnu štetu izravno izazvanu radnjama Bolta, što je teško zamislivo u praksi. Još je manja vjerojatnost da bi Grad mogao uspješno tražiti naknadu nematerijalne štete – za to bi morao dokazati da je Bolt namjerno kršio ugovor, i da je zbog toga Gradu nastala konkretna šteta, što je u ovom kontekstu iznimno teško dokazati.

Ipak, postoje određeni rizici:

# *Mogućnost jednostranog raskida* – Grad može prekinuti suradnju u bilo kojem trenutku uz 15 dana otkaznog roka. U tom slučaju Bolt više ne bi imao pristup podacima o vozilima, što bi otežalo ili onemogućilo pravilno filtriranje narudžbi. Grad moze to uciniti bez ikakvog razloga i bez ikakve posljedice, tj. neovisno je li Bolt krsi odredbe ugovora ili ne.
# *Reputacijski rizik* - Slazem se sa Sanjinom interpretacijom– Ako aplikacija ne filtrira narudžbe u skladu s listom vozila koja imaju pravo pristupa zoni, postoji rizik od negativne percepcije Grada ili javnosti, iako Bolt formalno nije odgovoran za prometovanje vozila.
# U ugovoru trenutno nisu detaljno definirani tehnički formati razmjene podataka ni učestalost ažuriranja. Kako bismo smanjili taj rizik, unijela sam neke izmjene – primjerice, dodana je obveza Grada da podatke dostavlja *pravodobno*, a *način i format razmjene podataka bit će definiran u dogovoru s Boltom*. - vidite je li vam to odgovara.
# Također, ugovor ne precizira na koji način je Bolt obvezan spriječiti vozače bez dozvole da primaju narudžbe za Uže središte, niti u kojem roku to mora biti provedeno nakon što Grad pošalje nove podatke. Preporuka je da se s Gradom dogovori što se smatra dovoljnom i prihvatljivom mjerom – npr. da vozač ne može prihvatiti narudžbu dok god nema aktivni status za zonu, kako bismo izbjegli kasnije nesporazume ili različita tumačenja. 
# Ugovor ne definira kako točno, ni u kojem roku Bolt mora obavijestiti vozače o promjenama pravila. S jedne strane, to nam daje fleksibilnost – ne postoji propisani rok, pa se formalno ne možemo smatrati „u zakašnjenju“. No, s druge strane, to otvara prostor da Grad u bilo kojem trenutku prigovori da obavještavanje nije bilo dovoljno brzo ili dovoljno jasno. 
# Također, nejasno je što Grad smatra „zadovoljavajućim obavještavanjem“ – je li to dovoljno push notifikacijom unutar aplikacije, ili se očekuje dodatna komunikacija (e-mail, poruka, fizičko isključivanje vozača iz aplikacije itd.). Bilo bi korisno dogovoriti konkretan minimalni standard koji će Grad prihvatiti kao usklađenost s ugovorom, kako bismo znali koje interne procese treba postaviti.

Medutim, imajte na umu da sto vise detalja ugovorimo to si ostavljamo manje prostora za neka kasnija drukcija tumacenja i morati cemo se striktno drzati ugovorenih obveza. 

U nastavku dostavljam ugovor s manjim izmjenama. Potrebno je vidjeti sto zaista mozemo uciniti i na sto se obvezati s operativne strane i prema tome predloziti neke daljnje izmjene.

Labas [~accountid:712020:f2473ea6-a01f-4207-919c-160dbe10a686], teikiu atsakymus į klausimus:

* *Ar galime naudoti terminą „pavėžėjimo dovanų kuponas“ / „ride-hailing gift card“?*Teoriškai taip, jeigu kupone aiškiai nurodyta, kad kuponas galioja tik pavėžėjimo paslaugai. Terminas „dovanų kuponas“ yra teisiškai galimas, tačiau gali sukurti vartotojui platesnius lūkesčius (pvz., perdavimo galimybę ar taikymą kitoms paslaugoms), todėl saugesnis variantas būtų naudoti terminą *„pavėžėjimo kuponas“ / „ride-hailing coupon“*.
* *Ar šis kupono produktas atitinka teisės aktų reikalavimus „dovanų kuponams“?*
Kuponas turėtų atitikti teisės aktų reikalavimus, jei kuponas turi a) aiškų galiojimo laiką, b) konkrečią vertę, c) apribojimus (pvz., tik pavėžėjimui), d) nurodytą sąlygą, kad negali būti iškeistas į pinigus.
* Taip pat atkreipiu dėmesį, kad pagal Bolt Business T&C “1.7. _Kuponas – Verslo portale Kliento sugeneruotas kodas arba kodų grupė, kurių kiekvienas leidžia Vartotojui pasinaudoti Kliento daliniu arba visišku apmokėjimu už bet kokius mokesčius, mokėtinus už atitinkamoje teritorijoje teikiamas „Bolt“ paslaugas, ir kurie gali būti kartais koreguojami._ +*_Klientas gali generuoti Kuponus pagal Verslo portale nustatytus apribojimus, pvz., galiojimo šalį, jame esančių kodų skaičių ir vertę, galiojimo terminą ir kitą Verslo portale pateiktą informaciją._*+ _Klientas privalo sumokėti už kodus, kuriuos Vartotojai panaudojo „Bolt“ paslaugoms_.” - tai šioje vietoje ne iki galo aišku, kokie papildomi ribojimai nustatyti Verslo portale, gal [~accountid:712020:f2473ea6-a01f-4207-919c-160dbe10a686] žinai apie ką čia kalbama?
* *Ar nėra rizikos, kad „dovanų kuponas“ būtų klaidinantis?*
Rizika yra, jei terminas vartojamas be papildomos informacijos. Vartotojai gali manyti, kad tai universali dovanų kortelė visoms Bolt paslaugoms. Tai gali pažeisti reklamos ir vartotojų apsaugos reikalavimus. *Todėl, kaip ir minėjau, siūlau vengti žodžio „dovanų kuponas”, o vietoje jo geriau vartoti „pavėžėjimo kuponas“.*
* Taip pat reikėtų ant paties kupono būtų disclaimer’is, pvz., „_Šis pavežėjimo kuponas galioja tik Bolt pavėžėjimo paslaugoms ir negalioja kitoms Bolt paslaugoms (pvz., Bolt Drive, Bolt Food ar pan.). Kuponas nėra keičiamas į pinigus_.”. Toks disclaimer’is turėtų būti pateikiamas ir prieš įsigyjant tokius kuponus (nesu tikra, kaip jie platinami). Taip pat pagal poreikį disclaimer'į galima papildyti informacija apie kupono galiojimo trukmę, ar jis gali būti perduotas naudoti tretiesiems asmenims ir pan. 

Jeigu kiltų papildomų klausimų - let me know 😉

Short answer: 
The payment failed because the order had a decimal value KES 942.24. Decimals are not supported for Mobile Money payments. 
Payment was marked as failed in Admin, but actually processed by pawaPay. 

Long answer: 
The payment was successful because pawaPay does price validation and rounds the price to the nearest integer. However, since there is a price difference we did not receive a confirmation the payment was successfully processed. 
The payment would have been successful if the user would keep the Bolt app open while the payment is being processed. It would allow us to process it synchronously and get the updated price with a webhook. 

We have asked pawapay to issue a refund for the customer. Will be able to provide you an update once I hear back from pawapay. 

Cheers, 
Marten

*Klausimas:* Dėl duomenų valdytojo statuso – Jūs minėjote, kad esate duomenų valdytojas. Prašome pagrįsti tai, nurodant teisinį pagrindą, kuriuo remiantis prisiimate šį vaidmenį (pvz., teisinė prievolė). Ar yra kokio nors teisės akto ar Valstybinės duomenų apsaugos inspekcijos išaiškinimo šiuo klausimu? Atsižvelgiant į Bendrojo duomenų apsaugos reglamento (BDAR) 2016/679 nuostatas, EDPS gaires bei į tai, kad veikiate mūsų interesais ir mūsų vardu kaip duomenų valdytojas, manome, jog pagal mūsų susitarimą Jūsų statusas turėtų būti duomenų tvarkytojo.

*Atsakymas:* Kaip jau buvo minėta, atkreipiame dėmesį, kad „Bolt“ teikia paslaugas verslo klientams kaip nepriklausomas duomenų valdytojas. Šis vaidmuo aiškiai nurodytas „Bolt Business“ bendrųjų sąlygoų 4 skyriuje ([*nuoroda*|https://bolt.eu/lt-lt/legal/]), kur pažymėta, kad „Bolt“ ir verslo klientas veikia kaip atskiri ir nepriklausomi duomenų valdytojai kiekvienas savo duomenų tvarkymo atžvilgiu.

„Bolt“ pats nustato asmens duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir priemones, reikalingas platformos veikimui, naudotojų paskyrų valdymui, transporto logistikos optimizavimui bei saugumo ir teisinių reikalavimų užtikrinimui. Tokiu būdu „Bolt“ visiškai atsako už savo duomenų tvarkymo veiksmus ir užtikrina atitiktį taikomiems duomenų apsaugos teisės aktams, įskaitant BDAR.

Šiam klasifikavimui pagrįsti remiamasi Europos duomenų apsaugos valdybos (EDPB) Gairėmis 07/2020 dėl duomenų valdytojo ir tvarkytojo sąvokų pagal BDAR. Ypač svarbus 82 punktas ir pavyzdys „Taksi paslaugos“ (27 psl.), kuriame aprašyta situacija, kai skaitmeninė platforma pati nustato duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir priemones transporto paslaugų kontekste. Nors „Bolt“ nėra taksi operatorius, šis pavyzdys analogiškai pagrindžia išvadą, kad platformos, kurios valdo skaitmeninę infrastruktūrą, formuoja naudotojo patirtį, nustato duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir sudaro sutartis su klientais, paprastai laikomos duomenų valdytojais.

Pagal BDAR 4 straipsnio 7 dalį, „duomenų valdytojas“ – tai fizinis ar juridinis asmuo, kuris „vienas arba kartu su kitais nustato asmens duomenų tvarkymo tikslus ir priemones“. Pažymėtina, kad „Bolt“ apibrėžia, kodėl ir kaip yra tvarkomi asmens duomenys, susiję su vairuotojais ir verslo paskyromis – nuo naudotojo registracijos, buvimo vietos sekimo, sukčiavimo prevencijos iki sąskaitų išrašymo – ir taip atitinka duomenų valdytojo apibrėžimą.

Siekdamas dar labiau pagrįsti savo įsipareigojimus duomenų apsaugai, „Bolt“ yra sertifikuotas pagal ISO/IEC 27001 – tarptautinį informacijos saugumo valdymo standartą. Tai rodo, kad „Bolt“ ne tik formaliai prisiima duomenų valdytojo vaidmenį, bet ir įgyvendina aukšto lygio technines bei organizacines priemones, saugančias asmens duomenis, kaip reikalaujama pagal BDAR 24 ir 32 straipsnius (duomenų valdytojo atsakomybė ir saugumas).

Apibendrinant, tiek sutartinės sąlygos, tiek faktinė „Bolt“ duomenų tvarkymo veikla pagrindžia, kad „Bolt“ veikia kaip nepriklausomas duomenų valdytojas. Toks statusas atitinka BDAR apibrėžimus, EDPB gaires ir taikytinus teisės aktus. Todėl abi šalys – „Bolt“ ir verslo klientas – lieka savarankiškai atsakingos už atitiktį, įskaitant privatumo pranešimų pateikimą, teisėto tvarkymo pagrindo nustatymą ir duomenų subjektų teisių įgyvendinimą.

*Klausimas:* Kokie mūsų darbuotojų asmens duomenys bus naudojami platformoje (vardas, pavardė, telefono numeris, kelionės vieta ir kt.)?

*Atsakymas:* Jūsų darbuotojai turės pateikti tik telefono numerį (jis yra privalomas ir turi būti teisingas). Jokių kitų asmens duomenų pateikti nebus reikalaujama. Taip pat bus renkami kelionės duomenys: paėmimo vieta, laikas, kelionės atstumas ir pan.

*Klausimas:* Ar automobilyje bus vykdoma vaizdo ar garso įrašų registracija?

*Atsakymas:* Pagal mūsų vairuotojų bendrųjų sąlygų 4.3 punktą, vairuotojams aiškiai draudžiama be leidimo daryti vaizdo ar garso įrašus, teikiant pavėžėjimo paslaugas. Konkretūs minėtose taisyklėse įtvirtinti draudimai:

· filmuoti ar transliuoti vaizdo įrašus internete be leidimo;

· daryti garso įrašus automobilyje;

· fotografuoti ar filmuoti keleivius be išankstinio informuoto sutikimo.

Šie ribojimai įtvirtinti keleivių privatumo apsaugai ir laikantis taikytinų duomenų apsaugos įstatymų, įskaitant BDAR.

*Klausimas:* Ar 2 klausime minėti duomenys bus perduodami Jūsų pasirinktiems duomenų tvarkytojams, subduomenų tvarkytojams ar trečiosioms šalims?

*Atsakymas:* Atkreipiame dėmesį, kad „Bolt“ veikia tarptautiniu mastu, todėl asmens duomenys gali būti perduoti, saugomi ir (arba) tvarkomi „Bolt Group“ įmonių, subrangovų ar partnerių, vykdant sutartinius įsipareigojimus už šalies, kurioje yra klientas, ribų. Išsamią informaciją apie trečiąsias šalis ir šalis, į kurias gali būti perduodami duomenys, rasite čia: _Bolt Group Companies and Controllers lists_.

*Klausimas:* Ar duomenys bus perduodami už ES ribų?

*Atsakymas:* Kadangi „Bolt“ veikia tarptautiniu mastu, asmens duomenys gali būti perduodami, saugomi ir tvarkomi „Bolt Group“ įmonių, subrangovų ar partnerių, vykdant sutartinius įsipareigojimus už kliento šalies ribų. Išsamią informaciją apie šalis, į kurias gali būti perduodami duomenys, rasite čia: _Bolt Group Companies and Controllers lists_.

Perduodant asmens duomenis už ES ar EEE ribų, „Bolt“ imasi visų būtinų veiksmų, siekiant užtikrinti teisinių reikalavimų laikymąsi. Tuo tikslu “Bolt” taiko atitinkamus duomenų perdavimo mechanizmus: *tinkamumo sprendimus* ir *standartines sutarčių sąlygas (SCCs)*.

*Klausimas:* Kur yra duomenų centrai, kuriuose saugoma platformos informacija?

*Atsakymas:* Švedijoje, Airijoje ir Vokietijoje.

Mostly standard, with acceptable controller–controller and controller–processor split. ➤ _Ask_: Fix to clarify governing jurisdiction.

➤ _Ask_: Add language prohibiting profiling/ML use without prior consent.
# *Deletion timeline* – No defined post-termination deletion period.
➤ _Ask_: Add 30–60 day deletion window and ability to confirm.



*That said, we have 2 options regarding next steps:*
